main_body: Conical thatched hut: a large straw dome roof (rows 4-57) over a clay/mud wall (rows 58-77) with an arched dark doorway
top_band: Golden thatch roof, rows ~4-56, banded in light-to-dark yellow courses. It is a large sloped surface seen from above, ending in an overhanging eave line at rows ~54-56
evidence: Down the middle column the finial and thatch dome form a big roof surface. A lighter eave row at ~54-55 is followed by a dark shadow row at ~56-58, then the brown wall face with texture dashes and a grey stone base at rows 75-77. The door is inset, with a brown frame and dark interior, under an arched thatch hood. The roof reads as a top slope, as the reference roofs do, and the wall is a separate front face, so this is a valid 3/4 structure.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 tones (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep course lines) and per-straw tick marks. The left-to-right shading gradient adds depth. The outline is dark brown, tinted to match the thatch and wall, not black. The wall has mottled clay grain, horizontal dashes and a speckled stone base. The door has a frame, inner shadow and arch. Detail per tile is comparable to the reference houses, and nothing looks sticker-like or flat.
